# 'knitr' is a new tool we are using, and we will be using the same r project for this and next week's seminar

In the empty () for col, we can use it define levels like line 22
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

lul_d <- read_csv(
  '../data/life-under-lockdown-wave2-extract.csv',
 col_types = cols(
    col_integer(),
    col_factor(),
    col_factor(levels = c(
      'Nothing at all',
      'Not very much',
      'A fair amount',
      'A great deal'
    )),
    col_integer()
  )
  )
```
The col part is to identify what kind of data each column is in order for R to use the data correctly

# Descriptive statstics
kable command is used to make the graph easier to read
```{r}
lul_d %>% 
  ggplot(
    aes (x = gender)
  ) +
  geom_bar()
```
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  count(gender) %>% 
  kable 
```
binwidth = n, the n is the amount of space each category takes up
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(x = beliefs)
  ) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1)
```
kable(digits = n) command rounds the number to the decimal point of n
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Mdn = median(beliefs),
    M = mean(beliefs),
    SD = sd(beliefs)
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 2)
```
# Hypothesis
Gender is associated with mean number of misformation beliefs.

#Analysis
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  group_by(gender) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Mdn = median(beliefs),
    M = mean(beliefs),
    SD = sd(beliefs)
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 2)
```
filter command filters out the mentioned part of the category
the . in the data = . is the filtered data 
```{r}
lul_d %>%
  filter(gender != 'In another way') %>%
  t.test(
    formula = beliefs ~ gender, 
    var.equal = FALSE,
    data = .
  )
```
There are too few people who identified in another way for them to be included in the full analysis. Males had slightly more misinformation beliefs (M = 0.73, SD = 1.13) than females (M = 0.61, SD = 1.05), but this was not statstically significant, t(494.31) = 1.201, p = .230.
